subject: Data Structure and Algorithm
chapters: Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms
Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists

questions.text: Describe an AVL tree. Construct an AVL balanced tree showing balance factors and rotation operations (LL, RR, LR, RL) after each insertion for the following sequence of data: 15, 20, 24, 10, 13, 7, 30, 36, 25 (or 18, 27, 9, 11, 36, 54, 81, 63, 72).

questions.chapter: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists
questions.text: Define stack. Write an algorithm for converting an infix expression to a postfix expression. Convert the given infix expression to postfix showing the status of the stack after every step: A * (B + C) - (B ^ D) * A + E / F or (A * B * (((C ^ X + D ^ Y) + E / Z) * F)).

What is collision in hashing? What are the techniques used for collision resolution? Insert the keys: 62, 37, 36, 44, 67, 91, 82, and 31 into a hash table of size 10 using quadratic probing (or linear probing) where hash function h(key) = key % 10.

Define Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). Explain Kruskal's algorithm to find the MST of a weighted connected graph. Construct the MST for the given graph showing each intermediate edge selection step and calculate total cost.

Explain how recursion uses the stack data structure with an illustrative call stack diagram. Write an algorithm to solve the Tower of Hanoi (TOH) problem for n disks and draw the recursion tree for 3 disks.

questions.chapter: Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.text: What do you mean by asymptotic notations? Define Big-O, Omega (Ω), and Theta (Θ) notations with their mathematical definitions and graphical diagrams. Explain how time and space complexity of an algorithm are analyzed.

questions.chapter: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists
questions.text: Differentiate between linear queue and circular queue with suitable diagrams. Write down conditions for queue full and queue empty in a circular queue. Write algorithms for enqueue and dequeue operations in a circular queue.

questions.chapter: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists
questions.text: Explain how linked lists are used to represent and add/subtract two polynomial equations. Write an algorithm and program to implement addition of two polynomials using singly linked lists.

Create a max-heap showing each insertion step for data: 28, 24, 50, 36, 42, 58, 22, 56, 46. Use the same heap tree to sort the data in ascending order showing all intermediate heapify and deletion steps.
Write an algorithm for Quick Sort. Trace the quick sort algorithm step-by-step to sort the following numbers: 30, 25, 79, 19, 48, 28, 21, 44, and 110.

questions.chapter: Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.text: Define data structure and Abstract Data Type (ADT). Briefly explain why Stack, Queue, and List are called Abstract Data Types with suitable examples demonstrating abstraction and encapsulation.

Construct a Huffman code tree for the given set of symbols with their frequencies: A (35), B (18), C (10), D (20), E (9), F (8). Determine the binary code word for each symbol and calculate the average code length.

questions.chapter: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists
questions.text: Explain operations of stack and queue using linked lists. Write an algorithm to insert a node at the k-th position of a doubly linked list and delete the n-th node from a singly linked list.

Define Breadth First Search (BFS) and Depth First Search (DFS) graph traversal algorithms. Illustrate both traversals on a given directed/undirected graph with 6 vertices showing the traversal order and tree edges.

Explain deletion of a node having two children in a Binary Search Tree (BST) using in-order predecessor or in-order successor. Describe insertion and node-splitting operations in a B-tree with an example.

questions.chapter: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues, and Lists
questions.text: Evaluate the given postfix expression using a stack showing the stack status at each operand and operator token: A B C * + D E ^ / F G * - where A = 2, B = 3, C = 10, D = 5, E = 2, F = 4, and G = 6.
